text:
Morgan: Quick check — I'm worried our current trace schema doesn't distinguish KV/prefix cache hits from full model invocations, which screws up cost attribution. We get token counts from model spans but cached responses look identical. Ideas?

Priya: 100%. We need something lightweight on the edge so we can tag hits without inflating envelope size. Also think about cardinality (no raw keys in spans). :thinking_face:

Sam: Are we planning to sample cache-only requests at the same rate? If they are high-volume, we could skew observability and cost signals.

Jin: Proposal: add three minimal span attributes on the request span: `trace.cache.hit` (bool), `trace.cache.type` (enum: kv|prefix|ttl), and `trace.cache.id` (8-char hex hash). Example: ```{"trace.cache.hit": true, "trace.cache.type": "kv", "trace.cache.id": "a3f4c9b2"}``` Keeps size tiny and avoids leaking keys.

Morgan: Hashing the key is smart. We still need a way to attribute cost to downstream owners (cache layer vs model infra). Maybe a separate enrichment event that joins on `request_id` and adds `cost.token_count` when model actually runs.

Priya: Tradeoff: enriching later means some traces won't have the full picture unless we do a join on request_id in the pipeline. That's extra complexity but keeps edge minimal. Alternatively, edge could emit `cache.meta` envelope with a tiny payload for offline joins.

Sam: If we go with delayed enrichment, we must guarantee eventual consistency for billing reports. Suggestion: write enrichment events to the same envelope fanout but to a low-QPS topic and mark them with `enrichment.v=1`. Also make sampling-aware: if a trace is sampled for debugging, force enrichment for that request.

Jin: Concern: cardinality explosion if we put too many enums or free-form tags. Limit types to the enum and hashed id only. No user IDs or raw keys. For joins, use `request_id` and `cache.id` only.

Morgan: OK decision sketch: 1) Add `trace.cache.hit` (bool), `trace.cache.type` (enum), `trace.cache.id` (8-char hex) at edge. 2) Edge emits tiny `cache_enrich` envelope event (request_id, cache.id, cache.type, sampled flag) to enrichment topic. 3) Enrichment job joins with model-span stream and emits `cost.attribution` record with token counts and owner tag. 4) Sampling rules: if trace sampled for debug -> force enrichment writes and set high retention.

Priya: Implementation notes: keep `cache_enrich` JSON < 256 bytes, checksum it, and add schema version `cache_enrich.v=1`. We'll add an opt-out for private customers (PII concerns).

Sam: Ops: we need a migration/backfill plan — retroactively compute cost attribution for last 30d from model logs where possible. Add a mitigation if enrichment lag > 10m to mark costs provisional.

Jin: I'll draft the minimal schema and a lightweight producer library for edge services. Will post an RFC PR later this week.

Morgan: Nice. Action items: Jin -> RFC + producer lib; Priya -> retention/opt-out policy docs; Sam -> backfill/migration playbook; I'll update the telemetry schema registry. @Priya @Sam please ack. :slightly_smiling_face:
